Milota Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Milota, Hungary

Demolished. Milota's cemetery was established as early as 1895, per that year's cadastral map; most of its territory is now overtaken by Christian graves from the adjacent local cemetery. The Jewish population reached 40 by 1910, but had fallen to just two families by 1944; the community had come under the jurisdiction of the Fehérgyarmat Jewish community from 1885. The only known survivor of Milota's Jewish community had emigrated to South America before the Holocaust began. By 1945, no Jews remained in the village; per the Yad Vashem database, about 10 were murdered in the Holocaust.
